The Framingham Study suggested a more than two- fold increased risk of stroke in women using menopausal HRT.1 However, subsequent studies reporting risk of stroke separately from other cardiovascular events showed either no effect on risk2 or a decreased risk in the order of 30 to 50%.3,4 Data from the Nurses’ Health Study cohort5 revealed little asso- ciation between the risk of stroke of any type and current use of unopposed oestrogens or oestrogen plus progestogen. However, they reported a trend towards an increased risk of stroke in cur- rent users of high-dose oestrogen therapy (1.25 mg or higher).
